advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the EXCLUDED_JOBS comment to quote the guard exactly (`github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`, not bare `'workflow_dispatch'`) so it is not a copy-paste trap.
advisory.finding: The EXCLUDED_JOBS justification comment paraphrases the job guard as `if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || 'workflow_dispatch'`, which is not a valid-equivalent GitHub Actions expression (a bare string literal `'workflow_dispatch'` is always truthy, so this abbreviated form would fire on every event). The real YAML uses the correct `github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`. A reader trusting the comment could copy the broken abbreviation.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the comment to: `if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the doc-link sweep's result distinguishable (e.g. drop `continue-on-error` while keeping the job out of vote.needs, or emit a step-summary annotation on failure) so a broken link is not indistinguishable from a clean/never-ran result.
evidence: .github/workflows/test.yml (sweep-doc-links step): "fail: false" combined with job-level "continue-on-error: true"

Comment claims: 'a link failure is a visible finding, never a gate (`fail: false` plus `continue-on-error`)' — but with both, a broken link and a clean run and a lychee crash all yield the same green job status.
advisory.finding: sweep-doc-links combines `fail: false` on the lychee action with job-level `continue-on-error: true`, so a genuinely broken external link never surfaces in the job conclusion — the job is green whether it ran and found no broken links, ran and found broken links, or lychee failed to execute. The 'visible finding for the CI owner' relies entirely on someone reading the step log; there is no distinguishable signal.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the sweep-interpreters 3.14 locked-cell extras (`dev+reviewbot+ui`) with the ticket's stated 'fewer extras than the gate / no ui/reviewbot' intent.
evidence: .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:355: `uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra reviewbot --extra ui --python '${{ matrix.python-version }}'` (the gate installs the identical extra set)

AC clause: 'The 3.14-stable and sweep-lower-bounds cells do NOT set REBAR_REQUIRE_EXTRAS (they install fewer extras than the gate ... and rely on importorskip self-skips)'; plan: '(uv sync --locked / .[dev,agents], no ui/reviewbot)'
advisory.finding: The `sweep-interpreters` 3.14 locked cell installs `--extra dev --extra reviewbot --extra ui` — the SAME extra set the Verified gate installs — contradicting the ticket's explicit intent that this cell installs FEWER extras than the gate (no ui/reviewbot) and therefore leaves REBAR_REQUIRE_EXTRAS unset to rely on importorskip self-skips.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin `actions/checkout` to a commit SHA (with a version comment) to match the SHA-pinning discipline used for setup-uv and lychee.
evidence: `- uses: actions/checkout@v7` appears in sweep-interpreters, sweep-windows, sweep-macos-full, sweep-lower-bounds, and sweep-doc-links

Same file comment: "new third-party actions are pinned regardless (epic 5664 S2 precedent)" while setup-uv and lychee are SHA-pinned (`astral-sh/setup-uv@ae62891...`, `lycheeverse/lychee-action@e7477775...`)
`uv pip install '.[dev,reviewbot,ui]'` in sweep-windows and sweep-macos-full
Only the 3.14 locked cell uses `uv sync --locked`; comment: "re-resolve latest"
No accompanying pyproject.toml change in the diff to confirm the `agents` optional-dependency group and its version floors exist
advisory.finding: New `actions/checkout@v7` usages in the sweep jobs are pinned to a mutable major tag rather than a commit SHA, inconsistent with the SHA-pinning discipline the same diff states it follows for third-party actions.
merged_from: The pre-release, Windows, macOS-full, and lower-bound sweep jobs install via `uv pip install` (re-resolution to latest / lowest-direct) rather than the committed lock, so their transitive dependency set is unpinned and non-reproducible run-to-run.
The lower-bound sweep references a `.[dev,agents]` extra whose existence and declared floors are assumed but not verified in this change.
